lemnos-alexandria-troas-to-thessalonica-.label: Lemnos via Alexandria Troas
lemnos-alexandria-troas-to-thessalonica-.synopsis: Galen's first Lemnian-earth voyage (SMT 9.1). En route from Asia to Rome, he sails from Alexandria Troas to Lemnos aboard a Thessalonica-bound ship, arriving at the wrong city before walking to Hephaistia for the earth itself.

sites.notes: Multi-word toponym; the Galen surface forms always pair Alexandria with Troad. Override exists because the auto-detector resolves 'Ἀλεξάνδρεια' alone to 20 ambiguous Pleiades records and 'Τρῳάς' to the broader Troad region — neither is right for the embarkation port in SMT 1/2.
sites.evidence_phrase: ἔπλευσα πρότερον ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος Ἀλεξανδρείας εἰς Λῆμνον
sites.narrative_note: The named departure port for the Lemnos crossing.

sites.notes: The destination of Galen's main Lemnian-earth voyage. Pleiades 550693 is the island record.
sites.evidence_phrase: οὐκ ὤκνησα πλεῦσαι, θεασόμενος ὁπόσον μίγνυται τοῦ αἵματος τῇ γῇ
sites.narrative_note: Galen lands on Lemnos at the wrong city; he intended Hephaistia but the captain put in elsewhere.

sites.notes: City on Lemnos; the actual collection point for Lemnian earth in SMT 1/2. Galen uses both 'Ἡφαιστιάς' and 'Ἡφαιστία' forms.
sites.evidence_phrase: τὴν Ἡφαιστιάδα διαγινώσκων τὴν θέσιν αὐτῆς
sites.narrative_note: The actual collection city for Lemnian earth — only learned by Galen on this trip that the island has two cities.

lemnos-italy-to-troas-via-thasos.label: Lemnos via Italy → Thasos → Troas
lemnos-italy-to-troas-via-thasos.synopsis: Galen's second, methodically-documented Lemnos voyage (SMT 9.1, b). He records the precise itinerary — Italy, Macedonia, Philippi, the neighboring coast, Thasos, Lemnos, Hephaistia, back to Alexandria Troas — explicitly so that future readers can replicate the trip.

sites.notes: The auto-detector treats Φίλιππος as a person (king of Macedon) and filters it. This override forces the place mapping for the dative 'ἐν Φιλίπποις' in SMT 2.

sites.narrative_note: Embarkation city after walking through Macedonia. Galen explicitly records the 120-stade descent to the nearby coast.

sites.notes: Stop on the Italy → Lemnos voyage in SMT 9.1 (b).

cyprus-soloi-mines.label: Cyprus / Soloi mines
cyprus-soloi-mines.synopsis: Galen's autoptic visit to the imperial copper mines at Soloi on Cyprus (SMT 9.3, with retrospective summary in De antidotis 1.2). The passages document a single in-situ stay: he speaks with the mine steward, observes the three concentric mineral bands (sory, chalcitis, misy), collects cadmia and chalcanthon for transport back to Asia and Rome, and revisits the chalcanthon → chalcitis transformation in his samples thirty years later.

sites.notes: Cyprus, not the Cilician Soli. Disambiguates against Pleiades's other 'Soloi' (Cilicia). The genitive Σόλων (also = 'of Solon') is the form Galen uses; CLTK can't lemmatize it correctly without context, hence the explicit override.
sites.evidence_phrase: ἐν γοῦν τοῖς Σόλοις … καθ' ὃν ἐγὼ χρόνον ἐπεδήμησα τῇ νήσῳ
sites.narrative_note: The single primary stop. Multiple anchors document the same stay: SMT 9.3 (K. XII 214.5, 219.5, 226.7, 238.1×2) and De antidotis 1.2.

sites.notes: Lock the bare-Cyprus mention to the island record (707498), not the Roman province (981516) or other variants. Galen's phrasing — 'to Cyprus for the mines' — is geographical, not administrative.

coele-syria-dead-sea-materials.label: Coele Syria / Dead Sea materials
coele-syria-dead-sea-materials.synopsis: Galen's investigation of the asphalt-bearing zone of Coele Syria — the eastern hill ringing the Dead Sea — for both ἄσφαλτος and the bituminous black stones that smell like asphalt. Anchored by SMT 9.1 (Coele Syria mention as motivation) and SMT 9.2 (the stones brought back). De antidotis 1.2 supplies the related Palestinian-Syrian opobalsam acquisition.

sites.notes: Multi-word region label; the κοίλη qualifier is lowercased in the TEI so the auto-detector can't catch it as a single proper noun. The override prevents 'Συρία' alone from defaulting to one of the six ambiguous Pleiades 'Syria' records.
sites.evidence_phrase: εἴς τε τὴν κοίλην Συρίαν, μόριον οὖσαν τῆς Παλαιστίνης, ἕνεκεν ἀσφάλτου … ἐπορεύθην
sites.narrative_note: Galen names Coele Syria as one of his three primary materia-medica destinations alongside Cyprus and Lemnos.

sites.notes: A 'complex-designator' toponym: Galen names the Dead Sea via the descriptive phrase 'the so-called dead sea' (νεκρὰν ὀνομαζομένην θάλασσαν), not a single capitalized noun, so the survey's standard tokenizer misses it. The full phrase is registered as an `ancient_names_in_galen` surface so the multi-word lookup in scripts/galen/survey_routes.py picks it up. See docs/galen_route_decisions.md § 'Complex designators' for the broader pattern.
sites.evidence_phrase: ἐν τῷ λόφῳ γεννωμένας τῷ περιέχοντι τὴν νεκρὰν ὀνομαζομένην θάλασσαν
sites.narrative_note: The 'so-called Dead Sea' — Galen's term, in the eastern part of Coele Syria, where both asphalt and the bituminous stones come from.

sites.notes: Pleiades has 3 separate Palaestina province records (I/II/III); using Palaestina I as the canonical pin since Galen's mention is general. Treated as context within the coele-syria-dead-sea-materials route.

pergamum-ergasteria-mines.label: Pergamum → Ergasteria mines
pergamum-ergasteria-mines.synopsis: A short overland trip on Galen's home turf: from Pergamum east-northeast to the mining village of Ergasteria, 440 stades distant, where he observed scattered molybdaina (galena) on the road. The lone passage anchoring this route (SMT 9.3 K. XII 229.7–230.4) supplies the named departure point, the named destination, and an explicit stadia distance.

sites.notes: Galen's birthplace; departure point for the Pergamum → Ergasteria mining trip (SMT 9.3 K. XII 229.7).
sites.evidence_phrase: κατὰ τὴν εἰς Ἐργαστήρια φέρουσαν ὁδὸν ἀπὸ Περγάμου
sites.narrative_note: Galen's home city; the named departure point.

sites.notes: Mining settlement near Pergamum. Until this override 'Ἐργαστήρια' was being filtered as a generic noun ('workshops') by the survey stoplist; the override re-promotes it to a place because it is the actual destination of the Pergamum trip in SMT 6.
sites.evidence_phrase: καλεῖται δ' Ἐργαστήρια κώμη τις, ἐν ᾗ καὶ μέταλλά ἐστι, μεταξὺ Περγάμου καὶ Κυζίκου, σταδίους ἀπέχουσα Περγάμου τετρακοσίους τεσσαράκοντα
sites.narrative_note: Mining village 440 stades from Pergamum, between Pergamum and Cyzicus; Galen observed molybdaina on the approach road.

sites.notes: City on the Propontis; appears as context in the Pergamum → Ergasteria passage (SMT 9.3) and as a place Galen comments on minerals (De antidotis 1.10).
